analysis: The only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md is a single added documentation bullet at head line 1025. It says App Attest serving authorization can remain visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM removal advice needs a matching fresh coordinator decision, and it links to provider-authorization.md. The supplied units are base_text covering lines 1-804 only. The added line at head 1025 is visible only in the patch excerpt, not in the numbered text. I examined the base text and the patch against the canonical threat model, including TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-057 and the related authorization and receipt language. The change is documentation only. It adds no code, endpoint, key handling or authorization logic, and it does not alter any receipt policy. The sentence is consistent with the model's statements that authorization is expiring and bound to a connection, and that backend policy is platform-owned. It does not claim that a cached verdict is an authorization grant, and it does not weaken the requirement for a fresh decision before MDM removal advice. Unverified: the referenced ../reference/provider-authorization.md file is not in the supplied evidence, and the doctor implementation that separates the two summaries is not supplied. The documented behavior cannot be confirmed against code. This is a documentation accuracy question rather than a demonstrated security regression. Other base content (logout revocation, cache settings, switch drain) is unchanged and was not re-reviewed beyond orientation.
